taskVersion.name: deadline-math-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Standard set, reasoning allowed. Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time: day rollover, the weeks when the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

ET refers to Eastern Time in the United States, which is typically UTC-5 during standard time and UTC-4 during daylight saving time. In 2026, September 30 falls during daylight saving time in the Eastern Time zone (EDT, UTC-4).

Madrid, Spain, is in the Central European Time (CET) zone, which is UTC+1 during standard time and UTC+2 during daylight saving time. In September 2026, Madrid will be on Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2.

So, the time difference between EDT (UTC-4) and CEST (UTC+2) is 6 hours. When it is 5:00 PM ET on September 30, 2026, it will be 11:00 PM in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

UTC is 5 hours ahead of Lima, Peru (which is in the PET time zone, UTC-5). So, when it is 12:00 UTC on July 15, 2026, it will be 7:00 AM in Lima.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00 (24-hour clock, my local time)

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CEST (Central European Summer Time) is UTC+2. Tokyo time is JST (Japan Standard Time), which is UTC+9. This means Tokyo is 7 hours ahead of CEST.

If the deadline is June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST, we add 7 hours to convert to JST.

9:00 AM CEST + 7 hours = 4:00 PM JST on the same day.

So, the deadline in Tokyo time is June 1, 2026 at 16:00.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PDT (Pacific Daylight Time) is UTC-7. Madrid, Spain is in the CEST (Central European Summer Time) zone during October, which is UTC+2. This means Madrid is 9 hours ahead of PDT.

October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT  
= October 12, 2026 at 08:59 AM UTC  
= October 12, 2026 at 10:59 AM CEST (Madrid time)

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 10:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PST (Pacific Standard Time) is UTC-8. Madrid, Spain is typically on Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1, or Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2, depending on the time of year.

March 3, 2026 is during standard time in Europe (DST starts March 30, 2026), so Madrid will be on CET (UTC+1).

11:59 PM PST on March 3, 2026 is:
- 7:59 AM UTC on March 4, 2026 (since PST is UTC-8)
- Then convert to CET (UTC+1): 7:59 AM UTC → 8:59 AM CET

So the deadline in Madrid local time is 8:59 AM on March 4, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET (Central European Time) is typically UTC+1. Los Angeles is in the Pacific Time Zone, which is UTC-8 during Standard Time (PST) and UTC-7 during Daylight Saving Time (PDT). On February 2, 2026, Los Angeles will not have started Daylight Saving Time yet (which usually begins in March), so it will be on PST (UTC-8).

10:00 AM CET (UTC+1) = 9:00 AM UTC  
9:00 AM UTC - 8 hours = 1:00 AM PST

So, 10:00 AM CET on February 2, 2026, equals 1:00 AM PST on February 2, 2026, in Los Angeles.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

JST (Japan Standard Time) is UTC+9. Lima, Peru is in the PET (Peru Time) zone, which is UTC-5. This means Lima is 14 hours behind Japan.

May 5, 2026, 8:00 AM JST  
→ Subtract 14 hours: May 4, 2026, 18:00 (6:00 PM) UTC  
→ Convert to Lima time (UTC-5): 18:00 UTC - 5 hours = 13:00 (1:00 PM) on May 4, 2026.

So the deadline in Lima time is May 4, 2026, at 1:00 PM.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 13:00

When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is given in PT, which is Pacific Time (UTC-7 during standard time or UTC-8 during daylight saving time). October 28, 2026, falls during standard time, so PT will be UTC-8.

Madrid, Spain, is in the Central European Time (CET) zone, which is UTC+1. However, in October, Spain is still on Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2.

So, on October 28, 2026, when it is 11:59 PM PT (UTC-8), the corresponding time in Madrid will be 8:59 AM on October 29, 2026 (UTC+2), which is 10 hours ahead of PT.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 08:59

When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

ET refers to Eastern Time in the United States. On October 30, 2026, Eastern Time will be on EDT (Eastern Daylight Time), which is UTC-4.

Madrid, Spain, is in the Central European Time (CET) zone, which is UTC+1. However, in late October, daylight saving time is still in effect in Europe, so Madrid will be on CEST (Central European Summer Time), which is UTC+2.

Therefore, the time difference between EDT (UTC-4) and CEST (UTC+2) is 6 hours ahead.

9:00 AM ET on October 30, 2026, is 3:00 PM (15:00) in Madrid.

When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET (Central European Time) is typically UTC+1. New York is in the Eastern Time zone, which is UTC-5 during Standard Time and UTC-4 during Daylight Saving Time.

October 27, 2026, is after the start of Daylight Saving Time ends (which typically ends on the first Sunday in November), so New York will still be on Daylight Saving Time (EDT, UTC-4) on October 27, 2026.

18:00 CET (UTC+1) = 17:00 UTC  
17:00 UTC = 13:00 EDT (UTC-4)

So, 18:00 CET on October 27, 2026, equals 1:00 PM in New York.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is given in PT, which stands for Pacific Time. In 2026, Pacific Time will be on standard time (PST, UTC-8) after the first Sunday in November. November 2, 2026, is before the switch to standard time in the U.S., so PT will still be on Daylight Saving Time (PDT, UTC-7) at that time.

Madrid, Spain, uses Central European Time (CET) or Central European Summer Time (CEST) depending on the season. In November 2026, daylight saving will have ended in Europe, so Madrid will be on CET (UTC+1).

PDT (UTC-7) to CET (UTC+1) is a difference of +8 hours.

November 2, 2026, at 23:59 PDT  
= November 3, 2026, at 07:59 CET (next day, +8 hours)

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 07:59

When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is given in PT, which is Pacific Time. In 2026, Pacific Time will be PDT (Pacific Daylight Time), which is UTC-7. Madrid, Spain, observes CEST (Central European Summer Time) in March, which is UTC+1. Therefore, the time difference between PT (PDT) and Madrid (CEST) is 8 hours (Madrid is 8 hours ahead).

March 20, 2026, at 11:59 PM PT (PDT) = March 21, 2026, at 07:59 AM UTC. Adding 1 hour to convert to CEST (UTC+1) gives 08:59 AM. But wait — CEST is UTC+2 in March? Actually, in March 2026, daylight saving time in Europe begins on the last Sunday of March. March 20, 2026, is a Friday, so daylight saving has not yet started. Spain will still be on CET (UTC+1), not CEST (UTC+2). Meanwhile, the US observes daylight saving starting second Sunday in March — in 2026, that’s March 9. So PT will be on PDT (UTC-7).

So on March 20, 2026:
- PT = PDT = UTC-7
- Madrid = CET = UTC+1 (since Spain switches to summer time on March 29, 2026)

Time difference: UTC+1 vs UTC-7 → 8 hours ahead.

So 11:59 PM PT = 7:59 AM next day in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 07:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET (Central European Time) is UTC+1. Los Angeles is in the Pacific Time zone, which is typically UTC-8 during standard time and UTC-7 during daylight saving time. On March 25, 2026, Los Angeles will be observing daylight saving time (PDT), so it will be UTC-7.

March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET = 11:00 AM UTC  
11:00 AM UTC - 7 hours = 4:00 AM PDT

So, the webinar starts at 4:00 AM on March 25, 2026, in Los Angeles time.

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

12:00 AM ET (Eastern Time) on October 12, 2026, refers to midnight at the start of that day, which is 00:00 ET on October 12, 2026. Eastern Time is typically UTC-4 during daylight saving time (EDT), which will be in effect in October.

Madrid, Spain, is in the Central European Summer Time (CEST) zone in October, which is UTC+2. Therefore, the time difference between ET (EDT, UTC-4) and CEST (UTC+2) is 6 hours. So, when it is 00:00 on October 12, 2026 in ET, it will already be 06:00 on October 12, 2026 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The "AoE" time zone stands for "Anywhere on Earth," which refers to the last time zone on Earth, specifically UTC-12. This means the deadline is set at 23:59 in the latest possible time zone, so that everyone around the world has had until the end of their October 9 to submit.

Madrid, Spain is in the Central European Time (CET) zone, which during standard time is UTC+1, and during daylight saving time (called CEST) is UTC+2. In 2026, daylight saving time will be in effect on October 9, so Madrid will be on CEST (UTC+2).

Since AoE (UTC-12) is 14 hours behind CEST (UTC+2), when it is 23:59 on October 9 in AoE, it will already be October 10 in Madrid.

23:59 UTC-12 on October 9 → 13:59 UTC+2 on October 10.

Therefore, the deadline in Madrid local time is 13:59 on October 10, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is at 12:00 PM Pacific Time (PT) on August 14, 2026. Pacific Time is typically UTC-7 during daylight saving time (which applies in August). Madrid, Spain is in Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1 in standard time and UTC+2 during daylight saving time (CEST). In August, Madrid observes CEST, so it is UTC+2.

The time difference between PT (UTC-7) and Madrid (UTC+2) is 9 hours. So, 12:00 PM PT is 9 hours behind Madrid time.

12:00 PM PT + 9 hours = 9:00 PM in Madrid on the same day, August 14, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

IST refers to Indian Standard Time (UTC+5:30). Madrid, Spain is typically on Central European Time (CET, UTC+1) or Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2), depending on the date.

November 10, 2026 is in winter, so Madrid will be on CET (UTC+1).

11:59 PM IST on November 10, 2026 = 18:29 (6:29 PM) UTC  
UTC+1 → 19:29 CET

Therefore, the deadline in Madrid local time is 19:29 on November 10, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Nepal Standard Time (NPT) is UTC+5:45. Lima, Peru is in the Peru Time zone (PET), which is UTC-5. The time difference between Nepal and Lima is therefore 10 hours and 45 minutes (Nepal is ahead).

April 2, 2026, at 17:00 (5:00 PM) in Nepal time is 6:15 AM on April 2, 2026, in Lima.

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Adelaide, Australia is in the Australian Central Standard Time (ACST) zone, which is UTC+9:30. Madrid, Spain uses Central European Time (CET) in winter and Central European Summer Time (CEST) in summer. In October 2026, Madrid will still be on CEST, which is UTC+2.

The time difference between Adelaide (UTC+9:30) and Madrid (UTC+2) is 7 hours and 30 minutes. Adelaide is ahead of Madrid.

So, when it is 10:00 AM in Adelaide on October 6, 2026, we subtract 7 hours and 30 minutes to get the time in Madrid:

10:00 AM - 7 hours 30 minutes = 2:30 AM (Madrid time) on the same day, October 6, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 02:30 (24-hour clock, my local time)

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney is typically in Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST, UTC+10) or Australian Eastern Daylight Time (AEDT, UTC+11) during daylight saving time. October is during Australia's daylight saving period, so Sydney will be on AEDT (UTC+11) on October 3, 2026.

Madrid, Spain, is in Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) in October, as daylight saving time will still be in effect.

The time difference between Sydney (AEDT, UTC+11) and Madrid (CEST, UTC+2) is 9 hours. Sydney is 9 hours ahead of Madrid.

6:00 PM in Sydney on October 3, 2026, is therefore 9 hours behind in Madrid time:
6:00 PM - 9 hours = 9:00 AM.

So, the deadline in Madrid local time is 9:00 AM on October 3, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 09:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).
